** Major** · **Stability & Availability** · **Quick win** **Recheck the trimmed length before slicing in `ellipsis`.** `ellipsis` measures the length before `TrimSpace` but slices using a bound that assumes the trimmed string is still longer than the limit. Whitespace-padded input that exceeds the limit can trim below `length-3`. The slice at line 205 then panics. Escape-sequence stripping makes this easier to hit: ANSI-wrapped padding now reaches this path. The same input with plain spaces already panicked before this change. Return the trimmed string when it fits within the limit. Slice only when it still exceeds the limit.
Suggested fix

```diff --- "a/pkg/api.go" +++ "b/pkg/api.go" @@ -196,14 +196,17 @@ } } func ellipsis(str string, length int) string { if length <= 3 || len(str) <= length { return str } str = strings.TrimSpace(str) + if len(str) <= length { + return str + } return strings.TrimSpace(str[0:length-3]) + "..." } // ansiEscapes matches ANSI CSI escape sequences (colors, cursor movement, erase) var ansiEscapes = regexp.MustCompile(`\x1b\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]`) ```

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Strip OSC sequences before storing diagnostics.** An error can contain an OSC 8 hyperlink around the visible text `failed`. OSC starts with `ESC ]`, but this matcher requires `ESC [`. For a short error, both hyperlink sequences pass through `TruncateError` and remain in `Status.ErrorMessage`. ([chromium.googlesource.com](https://chromium.googlesource.com/apps/libapps/%2B/HEAD/hterm/docs/ControlSequences.md?utm_source=openai)) Remove complete OSC sequences, including those terminated by BEL or ST. Preserve the visible label and keep the existing CSI handling. ([xtermjs.org](https://xtermjs.org/docs/api/vtfeatures/?utm_source=openai))

**Explanation** The title names the main change: ANSI escape codes are stripped from check messages and errors before they are stored. The change adds ANSI CSI stripping in TruncateMessage and TruncateError, which matches this. The title is 74 characters, within a normal length, and it is specific enough for a teammate scanning history.
Full details: Linked Issues check

**Explanation** [`#2386`] Requirement: remove ANSI escape codes from messages before they are saved to Canary CRD status. At head, pkg/api.go adds the regexp `\x1b\[[0-?]*[ -/]*[@-~]` (ansiEscapes) and stripANSI(). TruncateMessage and TruncateError now call stripANSI() before ellipsis(). The regexp matches CSI sequences such as `\x1b[90m`, `\x1b[1m`, `\x1b[31m`, and `\x1b[0m`, which appear in the issue's errorMessage example. Stripping runs before truncation, so the length limit applies to visible text. The test TestTruncateStripsANSI in pkg/api_truncate_test.go checks both functions with color, reset, and erase sequences and expects plain text. The PR objectives describe the controller's Status.ErrorMessage as using this path. I did not open the controller call site, so the write path into Status.ErrorMessage is established by the PR description and not by code inspection in this assessment. No coding requirement is left unmet on the evidence reviewed.

**Explanation** The whole-PR diff against the merge base changes only pkg/api.go (regexp import, ansiEscapes, stripANSI, and the two truncate functions) and adds pkg/api_truncate_test.go. Each change serves the ANSI stripping objective of `#2386`. No new dependency is added; the regexp uses the standard library.
